questions.q: What problem did multi-stage YAML pipelines solve compared to the old split of a YAML build plus a Classic Release pipeline?
options: They made pipelines run on faster hardware
They removed the need for any approval gates
They kept all deployment logic version-controlled in one file instead of splitting it across a YAML file and a separate visual designer
They eliminated the need for a build stage entirely
questions.explain: Multi-stage YAML folds both build and release logic into one version-controlled file, instead of leaving the release half in a visually-designed Classic Release pipeline outside source control.

questions.q: What does `dependsOn: Build` do on the DeployStaging stage?
options: It makes DeployStaging run before the Build stage
It makes DeployStaging wait until the Build stage finishes successfully before starting
It copies all variables from the Build stage
It has no effect unless pr triggers are also configured
questions.explain: dependsOn explicitly chains stages so DeployStaging only starts once Build completes successfully.

questions.q: What is a deployment job, and what is it always paired with?
options: A regular job that runs scripts faster; it needs no pairing
A job type (`deployment:`) built for releasing to a target, always paired with an environment
A job that only runs on self-hosted agents
A stage-level keyword with no relationship to environments
questions.explain: deployment: is a specialized job type for releases, and it's paired with an environment, which tracks deployment history and hosts approval gates.

questions.q: Where does a pre-deployment approval gate actually live?
options: Hardcoded as an `approve: true` line in the stage's YAML
In a separate pr trigger block
Configured on the environment resource itself, not written into the stage's YAML
In the pool section of the pipeline
questions.explain: The approval gate is configured on the environment (e.g. storefront-production), so it applies automatically to every run that targets it, rather than being written into the stage's YAML each time.

questions.q: For Northbridge Retail's storefront-api pipeline, what does the staging vs. production split achieve?
options: Staging requires manual approval while production deploys automatically
Both staging and production always require manual approval
Staging deploys automatically on a successful merge, while production waits on a lead engineer's explicit approval
Staging and production are deployed in parallel with no ordering
questions.explain: A merge to main deploys to staging automatically (Continuous Deployment), while production requires a human approval before the DeployProduction stage's steps run (Continuous Delivery).
